rules.title: Rent Ordinance just cause eviction requirement
rules.requirement: To evict a tenant from a rental unit covered by the Rent Ordinance, a landlord must have one of the 17 just cause reasons listed in Ordinance Section 37.9(a) as the dominant motive for the eviction. The mere expiration of a rental agreement or a change in ownership is not just cause.
rules.key_value: 17 just cause reasons under Ordinance Section 37.9(a)
rules.coverage_text: Rental units covered by the Rent Ordinance. This includes some tenancies exempt from the Ordinance's rent increase limits: newly constructed units that first obtained a Certificate of Occupancy after June 13, 1979, tenancies eligible for a rent increase under the Costa-Hawkins Rental Housing Act, and some tenancies where the rent is regulated by another government agency.
rules.penalty: If a landlord evicts or tries to evict a tenant unlawfully, the landlord may be subject to substantial civil and/or criminal liability.
rules.quoted_span: In order to evict a tenant from a rental unit covered by the Rent Ordinance, a landlord must have a "just cause" reason that is the dominant motive for pursuing the eviction. Note that the mere expiration of a rental agreement or a change in ownership does not constitute "just cause" for eviction.
